if dominos is changing their delivery fleet to electric is an example of what needs to be done first with EVs. fleet cars so, if dominos is doing what they're saying and converting their delivering fleet to electric. its a fairly good step, the numbers add up. theres roughly 5649 locations in the states. at 4 cars per location, thats 22696 cars lets say other brands follow suit. theres around 6500 pizza hut stores and around 3100 papa johns stores. all of these stores at 4 cars each, is around 60996 cars. thats massive. even at just 2 cars per location, thats around 35000 cars. and this is just a couple of pizza joints. you start to add in every food store you know does delivery, or every diagnostic truck or van on the road, marketing cars, etc. the number swells very fast and displaces a lot of ice cars. not everyone can afford an EV or lets face it, or wants an EV. but for a move to reduce emissions and inject a lot of EVs into the current market that will trickle down in time, and reduce carbon emissions. i do feel its a great move
